key_insight: SAGE improves NPU kernel synthesis by learning from which generated ideas were actually adopted, then consolidating only reusable hardware-specific knowledge into persistent memory.
engineering_relevance: This matters for accelerator software stacks because it reduces dependence on scarce expert tuning data while improving kernel performance on domain-specific NPUs.
method: ATU: assigns credit using both adoption traces and kernel evaluation outcomes.
UGC: keeps only high-utility, repeatedly adopted rules in a bounded resident context.
Persistent memory lets the agent reuse cross-operator knowledge instead of re-retrieving it each time.
evidence_signal: On NPUKernelBench, SAGE reached a 95.5% execution rate versus 84.1% for the strongest controlled baseline, and with GLM-5.3 it achieved a 43.99x speedup over torch_npu on sparse flash attention.
watch_item: The approach still depends on reliable adoption tracking and careful memory consolidation; noisy credit assignment or over-aggressive pruning could degrade retrieval quality.
paper_title: From Experience to Expertise: Adoption-Aware Memory Learning for Data-Scarce NPU Kernel Synthesis
